Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other
matter within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.
If you wish to address City Council, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers
and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during
discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. City Council will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda
during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council:
  ♦ Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  ♦ Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted
listening devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda
and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring

SUBJECT:  ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR MODERNIZATION OF ELEVATORS AT THE
  NORWALK/SANTA FE SPRINGS METROLINK STATION

Background:

On April 18, 2023, City Council approved an agreement with Schindler Elevator Corporation
(Schindler), to modernize the two elevators at the Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs Metrolink Station.
The project included furnishing all necessary labor, materials, equipment, and other incidental
work necessary to satisfactorily complete the project; including new control & power unit, valves,
wiring, door operator, door restrictors, door detectors, fixtures, and access switch.

The contractor’s work was satisfactorily completed on March 27, 2024 for the Norwalk east-side
and on March 29, 2024 for the Santa Fe Springs west-side. Both elevators were inspected and
passed by the State of California Department of Industrial Relations on the same day the work
was finished. The State inspector issued two temporary permits for the elevators so they could
be put into service immediate pending the issuance of permanent permits.

Fiscal Impact:

The project budget was approved for an amount not to exceed $159,976. A change order was
executed for additional work not covered in the Agreement for Fire Life Safety Upgrades. The
additional cost for the change order was $37,857.22.

The final cost of the project was $197,833.22 which was within the approved budget and funded
through Proposition C Local Return funds including a retention of $19,787.57 to be released to
Schindler after acceptance of work.

Background:

SUBJECT:  ART IN PUBLIC PLACES PROJECT APPROVAL - AQUATICS PAVILION

Background:

The City’s Art in Public Places Program provides a collection of permanent outdoor sculptures
and artwork throughout the City. Developments having a project cost exceeding five hundred
thousand ($500,000) dollars are subject to a one percent contribution to the program. The Art
in Public Places fund is used to create artistic enhancements within the community that fall within
the Program guidelines.

The Art in Public Places Committee (Committee) has reviewed a proposal from local artist,
Lindsay Parks, who recently displayed her work at the Mary Paxon Gallery and participated in
the City’s Artastic event. She has completed many mosaic projects, including several for the
Downey Unified School District where she is employed and included students and one for the
City of Downey. Her work consists of drawing out the design and then placing the mosaic pieces
to finish the mural. Since this piece will be placed at the pool, staff and the Committee asked
Ms. Parks for a design featuring elements having to do with water. Ms. Parks designed
a beautiful sea horse in the ocean surrounded by waving green underwater plant life. The
proposed design is attached to this report as Attachment No. 1. As part of this project, the
Committee is excited to announce that Ms. Parks was asked to involve youth from the community
to assist in placing the tiles to create the final design. The project will be shared through the
City’s social media and request youth volunteers ages 8-18 to participate in the project. Ms.
Parks will provide safety gear and instruction to the youth volunteers.

The piece will be comprised of three 30 1/2” x 88” panels placed between the two outdoor shower
enclosures as shown in Attachment No. 2. As the City is coming upon swim season the design
and accrual of the materials and pre-cut tiles will begin now, but the actual installation of the
piece will be in September after the Aquatic Pavilion becomes less busy. Design and scheduling
have been shared with the Parks and Recreation staff.

SUBJECT:  RESTORATION OF NORWALK TRANSIT SYSTEM FIXED-ROUTE SERVICE

Background:

Norwalk Transit System (NTS) currently provides municipal fixed-route bus service on six routes
within the southeast region of Los Angeles County including the cities of Artesia, Bellflower,
Cerritos, El Monte, La Habra, La Mirada, Norwalk, Santa Fe Springs, South El Monte, Whittier,
and unincorporated Los Angeles County.

On February 15, 2022, City Council approved NTS implementing temporary fixed-route service
adjustments, due to the COVID-19 pandemic creating bus operator shortages within the transit
industry as it related to the number of bus operators available to provide reliable fixed-route
transit service. These temporary adjustments included the following:

  •  NTS Route 1 – Reduced the number of assigned buses from six to five which resulted in
  the reduction in frequency of service (headways) from buses arriving every 30 minutes to
  buses estimated arrival times of every 37 minutes.

  •  NTS Route 4 – Discontinued express bus service which provided supplementary support
  to the regular Route 4 buses for commuter rail passengers to travel non-stop between the
  Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs Metrolink Commuter Rail Station and the Metro C Line
  (formally Green Line) Light Rail Station.

  •  NTS Route 7 – Reduced the frequency of service (headways) from buses arriving every
  45 – 50 minutes to buses estimated arrival times of every 60 minutes. Also, discontinued
  the shuttle service for passengers traveling between the El Monte Bus Station and Rio
  Hondo College.
 City Council  May 7, 2024
Restoration of Norwalk Transit System Fixed-Route Service  Page No. 2

Proposed Restoration of Service:

These temporary changes were enacted to reduce the number of bus operators required to
cover weekday fixed-route assignments and stabilize delivery of fixed-route service. NTS’
enhanced recruiting efforts and streamlined on-boarding process has filled most vacancies as it
relates to Bus Operators. This will allow NTS to restore fixed-route services in response to
patrons’ request for more frequent service as well as steadily post-COVID-19 ridership
increases.

Therefore, NTS is proposing the following:

  •  NTS Route 4 – Restore express bus service for commuter rail passengers to travel non-
  stop between the Norwalk/Santa Fe Springs Metrolink Commuter Rail Station and the
  Metro C Line (formally Green Line) Light Rail Station.

  •  NTS Route 7 – Increase the frequency of service (headways) for buses for estimated
  arrival times of every 40 minutes. Also, restore the shuttle service for passengers traveling
  between the El Monte Bus Station and Rio Hondo College will not be necessary based
  on current demand for service.

This restoral of NTS fixed-route services is tentatively scheduled to take effect Sunday, June 23,
2024.

Restoration of NTS Route 1 increasing buses to six in order to increase frequency of service
(headways) from buses to arrive every 30 minutes will be implemented at mid-year Fiscal Year
(FY) 2024/25.

Fiscal Impact:

The recommended fixed-route service adjustments estimated cost have been included in the
proposed FY 2024/25 Transportation Department budget.

Citizens Advised:

Outreach efforts to stakeholders and NTS patrons will include the following activities:

  •  Notice of restoration of NTS fixed-route services will be published in the Norwalk Now
  and posted on the NTS webpage, along with social media platforms.
  •  Airing of the restoration of NTS fixed-route services in English and Spanish on Norwalk’s
  cable television station.
  •  Notices in English and Spanish posted on all NTS fixed-route buses and bus stops.
  •  Letters mailed to stakeholders, including local school districts, elected officials, etc.; and
  affected municipal transit agencies.
 City Council  May 7, 2024
Restoration of Norwalk Transit System Fixed-Route Service  Page No. 3

Federal Transit Administration, Title VI Compliance, requires a public hearing and environmental
justice equity analysis for all service changes that meet the definition of a Major Service
Change. These changes did not meet the criteria for a Major Service Change, therefore, no
public hearing or analysis was required.

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 1, Provide High Quality
Customer Service to the Community Objective 1.1 Promote customer-focused culture that prizes
assessable, consistent and predictable delivery of service.

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council approve the proposed restoration of NTS fixed-route service for
Route Nos. 4 and 7; effective Sunday, June 23, 2024 and Route No. 1 at mid-year.

Background:

On December 11, 2023 staff issued an invitation for Bids for the construction of Firestone
Boulevard Improvements Project No. 7196. The project area is Firestone Boulevard from
Studebaker Road to Imperial Highway.

The project would upgrade the existing section of Firestone Boulevard from 4-lanes of traffic
(two in each direction) and a landscaped raised median to three lanes in each direction with a
center median. The project includes widening of the existing bridge segment over the Union
Pacific Railroad line and adjacent embankment slopes.

Furthermore, the project also includes multi-modal improvements with the installation of on-
street (Class II and Class III) bicycle facilities; traffic signal improvements; street lighting;
retaining walls to accommodate the additional roadway width; pavement reconstruction;
landscape and irrigation improvements; and pedestrian Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA)
improvements. Dual left turn lanes are planned at Studebaker Road, and Imperial Highway.
Numerous affected, existing driveways along with pedestrian ramps at the intersections would
be reconstructed.

The project is estimated to take two years to complete. For this project, the improvements will
occur in two stages. Stage 1 improvements consist of road improvements between Imperial
Highway and Studebaker Road with the exception of the bridge overcrossing of the Union Pacific
Railroad (UPRR). Stage 2 consists of the bridge overcrossing improvements over the UPRR
railroad right of way. On February 20, 2024, the City received 2 bids with the following results:
